title: SORNA section 20913(d): registration of pre-Act offenders
shortTitle: SORNA section 20913(d): registration of pre-Act offenders
summary: The provision authorizes the Attorney General to specify applicability and registration rules for people convicted before SORNA and others unable to meet the ordinary initial timetable.
notes:
The text must be read with the ordinary initial-registration requirement and the comprehensive-registration provisions surrounding it. In Gundy, the plurality construes the power as requiring registration of pre-Act offenders as soon as feasible, leaving transitional implementation issues. Gorsuch instead reads the provision as leaving fundamental policy choices about that population to the Attorney General.

Because the constitutional analysis depends on the scope of the delegated power, identify the competing statutory readings before evaluating nondelegation. Alito’s decisive concurrence accepts the result under existing precedent without joining the plurality’s complete construction. This is the text’s treatment in the supplied historical decision.
